blockA.interpretation: Block A improvement is entirely attributable to one trade, but removing it does not make the candidate worse than v4; it becomes neutral.

blockB.interpretation: Block B improvement is distributed across six changed trades; top contributor is about 30.6% of absolute delta mass, not a single-trade-only effect.

leaveOneOutSelectionAudit.interpretation: Under the frozen selection rule, removing any one eligible trade from Block A or B still selects horizon 5. This does not prove generalization, but it rejects the narrower claim that one trade alone determines the selected horizon.

acceptedConcerns: Block A performance uplift is single-trade concentrated.
The eight-horizon sweep creates selection risk because all horizons were evaluated on exposed development data.
Entry-price reclaim has not been established as uniquely structural versus alternatives such as VWAP or recovery-ratio definitions.
notSupportedByCurrentEvidence: Numeric claims such as 80% probability of fitting or 30-40% unseen reproducibility are not estimated by the current artifacts.

Bonferroni-adjusted significance cannot be asserted without a pre-specified inferential test and p-values; the current sweep is a deterministic development selection exercise, not a completed hypothesis test.

Replacing the current candidate with a 0.60 recovery ratio, VWAP OR rule, momentum confirmation, and horizon 6 would introduce several new unfrozen parameters without evidence from the current minimal sweep.

developmentDecision.reason: Among the tested minimal fixed-architecture horizons, bar5 is the only candidate with the highest positive worst-block delta and highest combined delta while remaining non-negative in both exposed blocks. It also survives 85/85 leave-one-out selection checks.
developmentDecision.nextAllowedUse: Use as the single frozen development candidate when genuinely new causal-valid data becomes available; until then, historical analysis may diagnose it but must not create a second competing candidate without explicitly reopening development.
